profile.reading:
This point is mapped as NTT Ashburn VA8, with an OSM-geocoded address in the 44700-44725 block of Gigabit Plaza, Ashburn, VA, on the same Gigabit Plaza cluster as NTT's confirmed VA3, VA6, VA7, and VA9 buildings. NTT does not publish a dedicated facility page for VA8, and its own campus index and overview pages list only VA1, VA2, VA3, VA4, VA5, VA7, and VA11 as named, page-linked buildings; VA8 does not appear at all in NTT's own public materials, though the address itself comes from public geocoded property data placing a real structure at that location. This entry does not assert a square footage or MW figure it cannot confirm from NTT's own site. NTT describes its overall Ashburn campus as 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley," a figure that necessarily includes whatever capacity VA8 contributes, even though NTT does not break that figure out by building for every address on the campus.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which large-demand campus buildings like this one face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision. NTT's individually documented Ashburn buildings offer a scale reference for a typical building on this campus: VA1, a few blocks away at 44664 Guilford Drive, is confirmed by NTT's own site at 64,723 square feet of raised floor and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load, though this registry does not apply VA1's specific figures to VA8 since NTT has not confirmed the two buildings match. NTT's own building numbering on this campus runs at least through VA11, and several numbers, including this one, currently lack an individually published facility page despite OSM survey data placing a real, named structure at the mapped address.

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA8 sits in Virginia's largest data center cluster, on Gigabit Plaza in Ashburn alongside confirmed NTT facilities VA3, VA6, VA7, and VA9. The facility itself has no published specifications; NTT does not list VA8 on its own campus index or dedicated facility pages, though property records confirm a real structure at 44700 Gigabit Plaza. Any capacity this building holds is included in NTT's stated 224 megawatts of critical IT load across the entire Ashburn campus, but the operator has not broken that figure out by individual building.

Virginia's regulatory environment has shifted sharply for this facility. In November 2026, the state approved new Dominion Energy rates that create a dedicated GS-5 rate class for data centers, requiring 14-year contracts and mandatory cost-coverage minimums starting January 1, 2027. These rates will reshape electricity costs across the Ashburn cluster, where NTT's documented buildings like VA1 (12.6 megawatts, 64,723 square feet) suggest the scale of individual structures on this campus, though VA8's own dimensions remain unpublished.

Whether VA8 matters to AI depends on capacity it has not disclosed. Of 330 mapped data center sites in Virginia, only 23 publish power figures, and they total 1,375 megawatts. If VA8 is significant, NTT should publish its specifications to let the grid and the AI industry plan accordingly; the omission itself is the fact worth noting.
